new_candidates.body:
## Summary

`RenderEngineGl::Clone()` shares the vertex buffers of deformable geometries with the original. A deformable configuration update in one engine therefore changes what every other engine in the clone family renders.

## Details

- Clones are created with shared OpenGL contexts (`internal_opengl_context.cc`, `Impl(const Impl& other)`), so buffer objects belong to the whole clone family; only vertex array objects are per-context.
- `DoClone()` copies `geometries_` and rebuilds the vertex arrays (`UpdateVertexArrays()`) on the *same* vertex buffers. Nothing distinguishes deformable geometries, so their `vertex_buffer` names are shared.
- `DoUpdateDeformableConfigurations()` writes the new positions and normals with `glNamedBufferSubData(geometry.vertex_buffer, ...)`, i.e., into the shared buffer.

## Consequences

1. Two clones (e.g., the engines in two different SceneGraph contexts) can't hold different deformable configurations; the last update wins for all of them.
2. Clones updating deformable configurations on different threads write the same buffer concurrently; a clone rendering on one thread can draw a partially updated mesh from another.

## Possible fix

On clone, give each deformable geometry its own vertex buffer (copy the data, e.g., with `glCopyNamedBufferSubData`) and rebuild its vertex array on the new buffer. The index buffer can stay shared since it doesn't change.
new_candidates.title: RenderEngineGl clones share deformable vertex buffers

new_candidates.body: ## Description A `ParticleField3DGaussianSplat` scene renders much blurrier (about 40% of the sharpness) when it's referenced into a stage that's already open than when it's part of the stage when it opens. Rendering a few frames right after adding it, before anything else changes on the stage, avoids the blur. This hits any app that builds its stage in code. Ours is a robot sim: `SimulationApp`, then `AddReference(scene)`, then robot and sensors. (Render Quality Below) *Top two rows: the same view of one scan, rendered by Isaac Sim RTX (stage opened from the file vs. scene added to an open stage), by 3DGRUT (3DGRT, 3DGUT) and by our sim's ZED X camera before and after the workaround. Bottom two rows: zoomed crops. Sharpness is the mean absolute Laplacian, with brightness matched across panels.* ## Environment - Isaac Sim 6.2.0 container (`6.2.0-rc.14+release.52805.02189a84`), headless, `RealTimePathTracing` - `omni.hydra.rtx-1.0.5`, `omni.usd.schema.usd_particle_field-1.0.0` - NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q, driver 580.178.04, Linux - Scene: 3DGS PLY (5.97M splats, SH degree 3; [superspl.at scene 38265403](https://superspl.at/scene/38265403), CC BY-NC), converted with `usd_convert_gsplat` 0.1.26, and referenced by a small Z-up wrapper USD with an `xformOp:transform`. 3DGRUT `transcode --format lightfield` gives the same data and the same result. ## Reproduction ```python """/isaac-sim/python.sh repro_particlefield_blur.py """ import sys scene, mode, out = sys.argv[1:4] from isaacsim import SimulationApp app = SimulationApp({"headless": True, "renderer": "RealTimePathTracing"}) import numpy as np import omni.replicator.core as rep import omni.usd from PIL import Image from pxr import Gf, UsdGeom ctx = omni.usd.get_context() if mode == "open": # the splats are part of the stage as it opens: sharp ctx.open_stage(scene) else: # the splats are referenced into an already open stage: blurred ctx.new_stage() app.update() stage = ctx.get_stage() UsdGeom.SetStageUpAxis(stage, UsdGeom.Tokens.z) UsdGeom.SetStageMetersPerUnit(stage, 1.0) UsdGeom.Xform.Define(stage, "/World/Scene").GetPrim().GetReferences().AddReference(scene) if mode == "added_settled": # workaround: render a few frames before touching the stage again for _ in range(5): app.update() app.update() stage = ctx.get_stage() # Pinhole camera, 105 deg horizontal FOV, ~0.9 m above the ground. Adjust eye/target/up to your scene. cam = UsdGeom.Camera.Define(stage, "/ReproCam") cam.CreateFocalLengthAttr(1.1124) cam.CreateHorizontalApertureAttr(2.88) cam.CreateVerticalApertureAttr(1.8) cam.CreateClippingRangeAttr(Gf.Vec2f(0.05, 10000)) eye, target, up = Gf.Vec3d(-1.054, -0.297, 0.877), Gf.Vec3d(-2.032, -0.392, 0.723), Gf.Vec3d(-0.137, 0.044, 0.99) UsdGeom.Xformable(cam).AddTransformOp().Set(Gf.Matrix4d().SetLookAt(eye, target, up).GetInverse()) rp = rep.create.render_product("/ReproCam", (960, 600)) rgb = rep.AnnotatorRegistry.get_annotator("rgb") rgb.attach(rp) for _ in range(90): app.update() rep.orchestrator.step(rt_subframes=8, delta_time=0.0, pause_timeline=False) img = np.asarray(rgb.get_data())[:, :, :3] Image.fromarray(img).save(out) g = img.astype(float).mean(2) lap = 4 * g[1:-1, 1:-1] - g[:-2, 1:-1] - g[2:, 1:-1] - g[1:-1, :-2] - g[1:-1, 2:] print(f"mode={mode} sharpness (mean |Laplacian|) = {np.abs(lap).mean():.2f}") app.close() ``` | Mode | Sharpness | |---|---| | `open`: stage opened from the file | 11.47 | | `added`: scene referenced into a new stage | **4.73** | | `added_settled`: same, plus 5 `app.update()` right after the reference | 11.48 | ## Observations - **Deterministic:** repeated runs give the same numbers to two decimals. - **Opening is fine:** opening a root file that references or sublayers the scene is sharp, and so is adding other prims after the scene has rendered. - **Re-adding blurs again:** deactivating and reactivating the scene prim makes it blurry again. `Usd.Stage.Reload()` keeps it sharp. - **Not the cause:** - time code metadata - `skipTonemapping`, `allHits`, `multiGpu`, `ecoMode` - render resolution - several render products, depth and motion vector annotators - lights - small camera motion - **3DGRUT reference:** rendering the same PLY from the same view with 3DGRUT's own renderers gives 15.7 (3DGRT) and 18.0 (3DGUT). Isaac Sim with the stage opened from the file gives 13.1, the blurred case 4.2 (same metric, see the image). ## Workaround Render a few frames right after adding the ParticleField, before any other stage change: ```python prim.GetReferences().AddReference(scene) for _ in range(5): simulation_app.update() ``` Opening the scene as the root stage also avoids the blur. In our app, though, `open_stage` after `SimulationApp` startup broke other render products: `[carb.scenerenderer-rtx.plugin] Failed to add HDR to LDR Tonemap`, and corrupt HdrColor-based images in a third-party sensor extension. ## Questions 1. Is this expected? Is there a supported way to add a ParticleField to an open stage without the blur? 2. Is the five-frame workaround safe to rely on? ### Isaac Sim version 6.2 ### Operating System (OS) Ubuntu 24 ### GPU Name RTX Pro 6000 ### GPU Driver and CUDA versions Driver 580.178.04, CUDA: 13.0 ### Logs _No response_ ### Additional information _No response_
new_candidates.title: ParticleField (3DGS) renders blurred when added to an already open stage
